tagline: Own your home, your servers, and your AI — curated by someone who runs it.
intro: A hand-picked kit for the overlapping worlds of the smart home, the homelab, the 3D-printing bench, and running your own AI. No scraped catalogs, no filler — every item here is something worth owning, with an honest one-line take on why.

author.name: Mike
author.credential: Certificate — Artificial Intelligence: Implications for Business Strategy, MIT Sloan School of Management
author.bio: I hold MIT Sloan's certificate in Artificial Intelligence: Implications for Business Strategy — and I actually build this stuff: ESP firmware, a self-hosted homelab, 3D printing, board-level hardware mods, and custom apps. Everything here is gear and knowledge I use, not a scraped catalog.

pillars.title: Smart Home
pillars.blurb: Local-first home automation. Bias toward Home Assistant, Zigbee/Thread/Matter, and gear you own rather than rent from a cloud.

pillars.title: Homelab & Self-Hosting
pillars.blurb: The boxes, drives, network, and software to run your own services and stop paying rent to someone else's subscription.

pillars.title: 3D Printing
pillars.blurb: Printers, filament, upgrades and tools that earn their place on the bench — tuned toward the Bambu ecosystem but not married to it.

pillars.title: AI & Local LLMs
pillars.blurb: Run models on your own hardware, and drive Claude & ChatGPT like a pro. The same 'own it, don't rent it' ethos as the rest of the list.

picks.name: Home Assistant Green
picks.blurb: The no-fuss way to run Home Assistant — plug in, power on, done. The default recommendation for anyone starting out.

picks.name: Home Assistant Yellow
picks.blurb: PoE, an M.2 slot, and a built-in Zigbee/Thread radio. The upgrade pick when you want one box on the network.

picks.name: Raspberry Pi 5
picks.blurb: Still the most flexible base for a DIY HA server. Pair with an NVMe HAT and it flies.

picks.name: Home Assistant Connect ZBT-1
picks.blurb: The SkyConnect successor — a USB Zigbee + Thread stick that keeps your radio off the main board and easy to relocate.

picks.name: Sonoff Zigbee 3.0 USB Dongle Plus (ZBDongle-E)
picks.blurb: The budget coordinator everyone recommends. Flash it, stick it on a USB extension, forget about it.

picks.name: Aqara Door & Window Sensor
picks.blurb: Cheap, tiny, reliable Zigbee contact sensors. The gateway drug of home automation.

picks.name: Aqara Presence Sensor FP2
picks.blurb: mMWave presence done well — knows you're in the room even when you're sitting still. Zone mapping is the killer feature.

picks.name: Everything Presence Lite
picks.blurb: Open, ESPHome-based mmWave presence board. The tinkerer's answer to closed-box presence sensors.

picks.name: SONOFF Zigbee Temp & Humidity Sensor
picks.blurb: Bench-tested: cheap, accurate Zigbee climate sensors with a display. Great for rooms, fridges, and the 3D-printing enclosure.

picks.name: Shelly Plus 1PM
picks.blurb: Relay + power metering that hides behind an existing switch. Local API, ESPHome-flashable, MQTT — the enthusiast favorite.

picks.name: ThirdReality Zigbee Smart Plug
picks.blurb: Compact Zigbee plugs with power monitoring at a price that lets you buy a ten-pack.

picks.name: Emporia Vue Energy Monitor
picks.blurb: Whole-panel, per-circuit energy monitoring for a fraction of the utility's price. Feeds beautifully into HA dashboards.

picks.name: Philips Hue
picks.blurb: Still the gold standard for reliable, fast smart lighting. Expensive, but it just works — and now speaks Matter.

picks.name: WLED
picks.blurb: Free firmware that turns an ESP32 + LED strip into gorgeous, HA-controllable lighting. The DIY entry point.

picks.name: Home Assistant Voice Preview Edition
picks.blurb: Local voice control with no cloud eavesdropping. The privacy-first alternative to Alexa/Google.

picks.name: ESPHome + ESP32
picks.blurb: The framework that turns cheap microcontrollers into custom HA sensors and controllers. Where the real fun starts.

picks.name: ESP32 (ESP-WROOM-32) Dev Boards
picks.blurb: Bench-tested. Dual-core Wi-Fi + Bluetooth for a couple bucks. Buy a 2-pack — you'll always want another.

picks.name: WeMos D1 Mini (ESP8266)
picks.blurb: Bench-tested. The tiny board behind my Wi-Fi thermal-printer build. Perfect for single-purpose gadgets.

picks.name: ELEGOO Breadboard Kit
picks.blurb: Bench-tested. Solderless boards in a few sizes. Prototype before you commit anything to solder.

picks.name: Dupont Jumper Wire Kit
picks.blurb: Bench-tested. M/M, M/F, F/F ribbon cables. You will use every one of these and still want more.

picks.name: 0.96" OLED Display (SSD1306, I2C)
picks.blurb: Bench-tested. Crisp little status screens for any ESP project — two data wires and you're showing readouts.

picks.name: Logic Level Converter (3.3V ↔ 5V)
picks.blurb: Bench-tested. The part beginners skip and then fry a board. Bridges 3.3V ESP pins to 5V peripherals safely.

picks.name: Silicone Soldering Mat
picks.blurb: Bench-tested. Heat-resistant surface with magnetic wells for screws. Saves your desk and your sanity.

picks.name: 37-in-1 Sensor Kit
picks.blurb: Bench-tested. A grab-bag of sensors and modules to learn with. The fastest way to find your next project.

picks.name: Beelink Mini PC
picks.blurb: Tiny, quiet, cheap x86 boxes that run Proxmox or Docker beautifully. The homelab starter that isn't a Pi.

picks.name: Minisforum Mini PC
picks.blurb: Step-up mini PCs with real cores and RAM headroom — for when one node stops being enough.

picks.name: Inovato Quadra
picks.blurb: A shockingly cheap ARM box that sips power — perfect for a always-on Tailscale/AdGuard/utility node.

picks.name: Synology DiskStation
picks.blurb: The most polished turnkey NAS. Pay the premium if you want storage that your family can use too.

picks.name: UGREEN NASync
picks.blurb: The value NAS challenger — strong hardware, and you can run TrueNAS/Unraid on it if you outgrow the stock OS.

picks.name: WD Red Plus NAS Drives
picks.blurb: CMR NAS drives built for 24/7 spinning. Buy from mixed batches, always keep a cold spare.

picks.name: Samsung T7 Portable SSD
picks.blurb: Fast, pocketable USB-C SSD — great for Time Machine, VM backups, or a bootable rescue drive.

picks.name: UniFi (Ubiquiti)
picks.blurb: Prosumer networking with a gorgeous controller. Once you VLAN off your IoT gear you won't go back.

picks.name: GL.iNet Travel Router
picks.blurb: Pocket router running OpenWrt with WireGuard/Tailscale baked in. The remote-access swiss army knife.

picks.name: Tailscale
picks.blurb: Zero-config mesh VPN that makes your whole lab reachable from anywhere without opening a single port.

picks.name: Proxmox VE
picks.blurb: Free, rock-solid hypervisor. The foundation most serious homelabs are built on.

picks.name: Immich
picks.blurb: Self-hosted Google Photos replacement that's genuinely good now. The reason a lot of people build a homelab.

picks.name: Jellyfin
picks.blurb: Fully free, no-account media server. Owns your movies and shows without a subscription.

picks.name: AdGuard Home
picks.blurb: Network-wide ad and tracker blocking. Point your DHCP at it and every device gets cleaner.

picks.name: Frigate NVR
picks.blurb: Local, AI-powered camera recording with real object detection — no cloud subscription, no monthly fee.
picks.program: None — monetize the Coral TPU + cameras

picks.name: CyberPower UPS
picks.blurb: Keeps your NAS and HA box alive through blips and lets them shut down cleanly. Non-negotiable once data matters.

picks.name: Phomemo D30 Label Maker
picks.blurb: Bench-tested. Label your cables, drives, and bins. The cheapest upgrade to a homelab you'll actually maintain.

picks.name: ARCTIC MX-4 Thermal Paste
picks.blurb: Bench-tested. The reliable, non-conductive default for repasting a mini PC, NAS, or GPU that's running hot.

picks.name: Bambu Lab A1 mini
picks.blurb: The best first printer, full stop. Auto-calibration means you print instead of tinker — unless you want to.

picks.name: Bambu Lab A1
picks.blurb: Full-size bed, same hands-off ease as the mini, optional AMS lite for multicolor. The value sweet spot.

picks.name: Bambu Lab P1S
picks.blurb: Enclosed CoreXY speed demon for ABS/ASA and engineering filaments. The upgrade most people land on.

picks.name: Prusa Core One
picks.blurb: The open, repairable, made-to-last alternative. Buy it if you value the ecosystem and want to own your machine.

picks.name: Bambu PLA Basic
picks.blurb: Consistent, RFID-tagged filament that the AMS reads automatically. The path of least resistance.

picks.name: Polymaker PolyTerra PLA
picks.blurb: Matte finish, great color range, eco-spool. A favorite for parts you want to look intentional.

picks.name: Overture PETG
picks.blurb: Reliable, affordable PETG for functional parts that need to survive heat and stress. The go-to workhorse.

picks.name: ELEGOO Rapid PETG
picks.blurb: Bench-tested (I go through this by the case): high-speed PETG that prints clean and cheap. My default workhorse spool.

picks.name: DEEPLEE PLA (2kg / 4kg)
picks.blurb: Bench-tested. Big-spool value PLA that winds neatly and doesn't clog. What I reach for when cost-per-gram matters.

picks.name: Bambu AMS
picks.blurb: Multi-color and multi-material without babysitting. Also just a great auto-feeding filament pantry.

picks.name: Hardened Steel Nozzle
picks.blurb: The five-dollar upgrade that saves your nozzle the first time you print carbon-fiber or glow filament.

picks.name: Filament Dryer (Sunlu S4 / Eibos)
picks.blurb: Wet filament ruins prints. A dryer fixes stringing and brittle parts — the upgrade people skip and regret.

picks.name: OrcaSlicer
picks.blurb: The community slicer with the best calibration tooling. Free, and better than most stock slicers.

picks.name: Digital Calipers
picks.blurb: You cannot design functional parts without measuring. Buy one decent pair, not three cheap ones.

picks.name: MakerWorld
picks.blurb: Huge, mostly-free model library with one-click print profiles for Bambu machines. Start here before modeling anything.

picks.name: Ollama
picks.blurb: Run open LLMs locally with one command. The easiest on-ramp to your own private AI.

picks.name: LM Studio
picks.blurb: A polished desktop app for downloading and chatting with local models. Great for non-terminal folks.

picks.name: Open WebUI
picks.blurb: Self-hosted ChatGPT-style front end for Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API. Runs beautifully on the homelab.

picks.name: Jan
picks.blurb: Open-source, offline-first AI assistant. Everything stays on your machine.

picks.name: Mac mini (Apple Silicon)
picks.blurb: Unified memory makes it a shockingly good, quiet local-LLM box. The value pick for running mid-size models.

picks.name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX (VRAM is king)
picks.blurb: For local AI, buy the most VRAM you can afford. A used 3090's 24GB still punches above its price.

picks.name: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano
picks.blurb: A tiny always-on edge box for running small models and vision at the edge of your network.

picks.name: Claude Code
picks.blurb: Drive Claude from your terminal to build, edit, and automate. The power-user way to work with Claude.

picks.name: ChatGPT
picks.blurb: Custom instructions + Projects + memory turn it from a toy into a real assistant. Learn those three and it changes.

picks.name: Cursor
picks.blurb: AI-native code editor. If you write code, this is the fastest on-ramp to model-assisted work.

picks.name: LibreChat
picks.blurb: Self-hosted, multi-model chat UI — bring your own API keys for Claude, GPT, and local models in one place.

picks.name: AI Engineering (Chip Huyen)
picks.blurb: The field guide to building real products on top of foundation models. Start here if you're going pro.

picks.name: Hands-On Large Language Models
picks.blurb: The best illustrated, practical intro to how LLMs actually work and how to use them.

picks.name: DeepLearning.AI Short Courses
picks.blurb: Free, focused, hour-long courses on prompting, RAG, agents, and more. The fastest way to skill up.

picks.name: fast.ai
picks.blurb: The legendary free, top-down deep-learning course. Rigorous without being academic-for-its-own-sake.
